## Plan landed (2026-10-20)

- **PR #296 merged** as `85f9145b` — the burndown is now canon in `docs/jev-roadmap.md` ("Completion burndown — 2026-10-20"), 12/12 CI green including audit. Branch deleted. This tracker is the execution state; the roadmap section is the canon pointer.
- **Every item below has an issue** with end state + acceptance criteria: Waves 0–4 are #276, #277, #278, #279, #287, #290, #284, #286, #270–#273, #282, #283, #285, #288, #289, #275, #280, #281, #291, #292, #293; Wave 5 is #294 plus the operator-held items listed in the body.
- **Board unblocked:** PR #296 also re-pointed the D12 coverage baseline at `0c4210f3` (traced refresh, 4,737 tests OK). The baseline had been pinned to the orphaned pre-squash commit `75f598c` from #274 and was failing D12 closed on *every* new PR — evidence on #276. #276 (merge-base measurement) is the permanent fix and stays Wave 0.
- One CI note: the macOS installed-package leg was cancelled once by a runner timeout and passed on re-run; all other legs passed first try.

Lane: start at Wave 0. One PR at a time, green merges.

## Tracker maintenance (2026-10-20): #297 added to Wave 4

**#297 "Unify Jev review and resumable lifecycle across task lanes"** (filed by the operator as a follow-up to PR #274) joins the burndown in **Wave 4 — product depth**: one typed lifecycle contract + coordinator for Jev review and resumable execution across the chat, audit, auto-edit, driver, and provisioning lanes, with per-lane regression coverage (no double-applied edits, no replayed provider calls, usage liability retained exactly once).

- [ ] #297 unified Jev review + resumable lifecycle contract (~400-600 LoC estimated; one PR per the wave rules)

The board is now 26 open issues (#270–#295, #297); the roadmap canon section is being updated in a small follow-up PR to keep its wave list accurate. The definition of done is unchanged.

## Verification findings added — 2026-10-20 full verification pass

A complete verification pass over main `dd83caf9` (pristine checkout: full suite 4,737 tests OK, CI 12/12 green incl. audit, plus live exercise + adversarial probing of the CLI, MCP, GUI, driver, refine, site-check, and site-export surfaces) surfaced five small, precisely-scoped defects. All are filed with verified file:line evidence and repros; proposed wave placement:

**Wave 1 (small robustness / CI hygiene, alongside #287/#290):**
- #299 — fix(server): cap POST body size before reading (`harness/server.py:1303-1304`; 64MB body buffered + parsed today; 413 over cap). ~15 LoC.
- #301 — ci: `driver_core` is outside the ruff scope; dead import F401 at `driver_core/osal.py:52` sits unseen on main. ~3 LoC + CI line. (Check against #292's v3.5.0 sync.)
- #303 — fix(site-check, minor): non-http(s) schemes in prose prompts bypass the scheme gate via extractor normalization (`harness/web.py:535` only sees the normalized URL). ~15 LoC.

**Wave 2 (driver block, alongside #270–#273):**
- #300 — fix(driver_core): `check_batch` docstring (`actions.py:253-258`) claims it refuses irreversible-mixed batches; the implementation (`actions.py:262-269`) only refuses >1 irreversible, and it has no production caller. Enforce the documented rule (preferred) or correct the docstring. ~5–40 LoC.

**Wave 4 (alongside #280, same structured-output-rotation theme):**
- #302 — harden(apply): screen refusal/non-code model output at intake (`harness/apply_policy.py:409-423` covers empty/reasoning-only; the refusal class is uncovered) and stop crediting model health `ok=True` for missing-marker responses (`apply_policy.py:443-448, 458`). Downstream gates caught the observed instance — zero bytes written — so this is intake hygiene, not a breach fix. ~40 LoC.

Everything else probed verified as documented and fail-closed; the pass's full report is with the operator. No wave re-ordering is proposed — Wave 0 (#276 → #277) still goes first.

## Addendum — #304 staged (Fireworks routing / EV-8 completion), canon PR #305

One more item from the operator, now fully staged:

- **#304 — feat(economics): include Fireworks in automatic cheapest-capable routing with dynamic price checking (completes EV-8).** Filed with the full verified gap analysis: `resolve_route`/`chat_for_route` have no production callers outside the probe (`harness/fireworks_probe.py:79, 97`); Fireworks prices are the static 2026-10-08 pack (`harness/endpoint_pricing.py:432`) compared against a second static snapshot (`harness/routing_table.py:203`); dynamic price checking exists only for OpenRouter. **Placed in Wave 4** alongside the other economics/calibration work (#280, #302). Its closing step — the EV-8 live call (≤$0.01, operator holds ~$6 in Fireworks credits) — is operator-gated in the Wave 5 sense: it runs only after the key is placed (`harness/config.py:601-621`) and the five written confirmations in canon's Fireworks confirmation list are given. Parts (a)–(d) of the issue need neither and can start with Wave 4.
- **Canon:** PR #305 adds #304 (Wave 4), #302 (Wave 4), #299/#301/#303 (Wave 1), and #300 (Wave 2) to the burndown section of `docs/jev-roadmap.md`, points the EV-8 row at #304, and adds an accuracy note to the EV-7 row (its selection sentence states the design target; production pool ordering doesn't consume it yet — #304 closes that).
- A lane-assist comment with sequencing, entry points, and constraints is posted on #304 itself.

With this, everything from the 2026-10-20 verification pass and the operator's Fireworks directive is inside canonical planning and staged in waves. Wave order is unchanged — Wave 0 (#276 → #277) still goes first.

## Addendum — EV-8 verification execution tasked: #306

[#306](https://github.com/Sovereign-Communication/harness/issues/306): the freebuff lane is tasked to place the Fireworks key (present on the lane's machine) into the harness config environment and complete the EV-8 verification in full — receipt, canon row flip, `jev-phase --phase EV-8`. The five confirmations are recorded as given on #304 (operator's word, 2026-10-20). This is #304's step (e) split out as its own executable task; it is unblocked now and independent of #304 parts (a)–(d) in Wave 4.

## Tracker maintenance (2026-10-20, 21:45 HST) — folding lane-initiative work into the board

So nothing is unaccounted: **PR #312** (install/auth/chat-recovery unification, 12/12 green on `750ca4f3`, operator-approved) merges now, ahead of Wave 0. Lane-filed **#308–#311** (provision trust-boundary split, evaluator/dispatch separation, `waist.py` split, local-fit hermetic CI) slot after #297's wave-4 position, in lane-defended order. **#306** stays first-item (lane-machine EV-8 verification — it blocks the EV-8 canon flip and is currently unacknowledged; nudge posted). Owner-gated exclusions unchanged: #294 flag flip (evidence work only, flags stay off), dogfood mission deployment, `feat/refine-loop-p0` unmerged commit triage.

## Reconciled audit-to-issue intake (2026-10-22)

All 99 existing issue records (open/closed; PRs excluded from issue listing) were checked before creating focused missing follow-ups. No tests, probes, paid model calls, implementation or workspace edits in this filing step.

### New focused issues
- #342 missing shared typed model-proposed ResearchPlan; bounded native review/revision before retrieval; actual CLI/MCP/GUI caller ownership. Source-confirmed missing functionality; cases7/8 are limited routing fixtures.
- #343 per-hit domain/semantic relevance: mixed on-subject + Microsoft mailbox results reached the answer (controlled case8). Distinct follow-up to merged PR #341's batch gate.
- #344 checkpoint context/route binding after changed or newly declined requests (controlled cases1/2; follow-up to closed #297).
- #345 concurrent request-cap accounting consumes another request's allowance (controlled synthetic case3; false refusal).
- #346 completed decomposition cost counted again against remaining allowance (controlled synthetic case4; final other-stage analogues source-only).
- #347 loader ignores disabling override / restores ambient key for None; failed CLI smoke5. Explicit JevEvaluator disabling itself is honored per inspected source.

### Existing owners reused, no duplicate issues created
- #308 planning ownership/large waist.py/duplicate budget assembly; #346 is its concrete correctness follow-up.
- #309 domain evaluators versus shared dispatch; idle research adapters are wired under #342.
- #277 authoritative CLI/GUI/MCP/site verification and evidence reporting. Detailed cases and exact missing evidence attached there.
- #282 GUI critical journeys; #283 dependent IPC coverage; #285 MCP tool/chaining evaluation. No GUI or installed-host parity proof was produced by the controlled stdio smokes.
- #290 hermetic environment triage; case5 distinction attached there.

### Evidence boundaries
Case6 passed the local controlled MCP schema/advisory-preview/cap-cleanup/ping flow; case7 passed answer-route zero retrieval. They do not certify installed MCP-host synchronization or complete ResearchPlan decline/approval. Live fetch9 returned HTTP403 (content unavailable), not a successful site audit. Case10 only verified dirty-file integrity/source references. Early case1-3 exit codes and separate stderr streams are unavailable.

Cumulative allowance is exhausted10/10 (nine behavioral cases including failed fixture5, plus final integrity/source probe10). Paid model/Jev total and defensible upper bound $0.00; synthetic accounting is not billing. No allowance is reset by filing issues.

Ready for canonical planning in docs/jev-roadmap.md: track dependencies between #342/#343/#344 and independent accounting/config repairs #345/#346/#347, then close evidence gaps under #277/#282/#285. No phase order, Jev gate result, implementation completion or merge is asserted here. Existing one-PR-at-a-time / independent Jev and CI completion rules remain in force.

**Planning receipt — 2026-10-22 (plan published for review, no issue closed)**

The full-scope implementation plan is now in canon for review: **PR #348** (`docs/issue-295-implementation-plan-20261022`).

**Coverage:** 61 live open issues → 61 plan rows (this tracker + 60 work items), each with owner, real contract prerequisites, a concrete acceptance exit, and inherited G0–G4 gates. Parsed graph: 74 dependency edges, no cycles, no dangling prerequisite. No shipped, closed or deferred row was reopened. **Next slice: #347 only.**

**Native Jev plan audit (4 bounded single-POST reviews, $0.001836 total, no retries, `is_fallback=false`, linked 4-row ledger chain):**

| Round | `proceed` share | Lead | destructive | advances_goal | Composer | v1 disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.44 | 0.09 | 0.04 | 0.74 | escalate | stop (ambiguity) |
| 2 | 0.44 | 0.14 | 0.04 | 0.78 | escalate | stop (ambiguity) |
| 3 | 0.69 | 0.46 | 0.04 | 0.75 | escalate | investigate |
| 4 | 0.81 | 0.68 | 0.04 | 0.81 | escalate | investigate-cleared → proceed (publication only) |

The composer's `escalate` in rounds 3–4 rests solely on the hard-coded `advances_goal < 0.95` rule, which ratified [JEV_GATE_POLICY_V1](https://github.com/Sovereign-Communication/harness/blob/main/docs/JEV_GATE_POLICY_V1.md) converts to *investigate* — that divergence is #324, and it is recorded, not papered over. **No mechanical green is claimed.**

**Investigation produced one real correction:** the earlier "stale installed MCP schema" finding is **withdrawn**. The installed runtime's `mcp_schemas.py` is byte-identical to committed `208c455` (sha256 `9a0e274a…05c7ab6`), so the 0.25 `max_cost` cap and the absence of `allow_heuristic_preview` are simply the committed state; both exist only in the uncommitted audit worktree. The implementable task is to land or re-derive that change in a phase PR — not to refresh a client.

**Still blocked, and by what:**

- **G1/G4 execution (any issue):** the functional verification allowance is exhausted at 10/10. Nothing can be implemented-and-verified until a fresh counted tranche is allocated (cases, budget, and which of CLI/GUI/MCP).
- **#347 → #346 → #345 → #344 → #342/#343:** the ordered path, but all sit behind that tranche.
- **#277 surface matrix** also needs #276/#331/#327/#330 landed, plus browser capability for site-level evidence.
- **GUI:** Python `pywebview` is absent on this machine, so GUI work starts from the loopback browser runtime — an access limit, not a passing journey.
- **Owner decisions outstanding:** #273 consent wording, #294's 50-validated-key run, #291's remaining 20 cycles, #306 one-shot state, and any flag flip or publication.

Access status: Jev key resolves locally; Harness MCP discovery is working again (initialize/list/ping) — **MCP is unblocked**.

**Follow-up receipt — audit gate restored, plan PR green**

- **#349** `fix(audit): re-point the D12 coverage baseline at main` — one file (`audits/self/coverage_baseline.json`), regenerated by the sanctioned traced run (`refresh_coverage_baseline.py`: 4815 tests, OK, 73 skipped, 470s), now pinned to `208c455` (an ancestor of main). `audit` **pass**; A/R/SM/SD all 10.00/10.
- **#348** (this plan) is now green on `audit` as well, stacked on #349 so its merge ref contains the fixed pin. Diff vs base is docs-only, 1 file; the reviewed plan block is still `a7282ad0…`.

Merge order if approved: **#349 first, then #348** (which auto-retargets to `main`).

Unchanged holds: functional verification allowance still exhausted at 10/10, so no plan row can move to implementation; macOS legs are queued/not-run on both PRs (no macOS runner has picked up a job since `main` at 09:53Z), so macOS remains unverified; #276's durable merge-base measurement is still the permanent fix behind this interim re-point.

The ... branch was force-pushed or recreated`). #350 carried identical content against `main`, so no review content was lost.

## STEERING — new commission: Saturation (Flush) Loop rows FLUSH-0..FLUSH-3

Owner directive (2026-11-04): add the flush-out loop to Harness, dispatched to this lane for the FreeBuff burndown. Slot the four rows below into the canon register **behind the existing #295 order** — this steering does not reorder any existing row. One phase PR at a time, repo gates as usual.

### What the Flush Loop is

A first-class audit mode that iterates a target (code, plan, prompt, live surface) to a *fixed point*, under this operator:

- **Rule 0 — never without changes.** No pass runs on an unchanged state; every pass carries a semantic delta (new evidence record IDs, a changed target hash, a new angle ID, or a new instrument ID — byte-level churn canonicalizes to the same information-set hash and the pass refuses to start). When a pass stalls on missing information, the loop emits an INFO REQUEST naming the exact missing record and parks only that aspect; adding the named information resumes it.
- **Saturation, per aspect**, across rotated angles (flaw-hunt, red-team, missing-evidence, production-failure counterfactual) AND rotated instruments (Jev diagnostics, a different-family panel, deterministic checks, non-author cold runs).
- **Gap register with no "noted" state:** findings exit only as CLOSED (cure landed + re-score on the changed artifact) or DECISION-READY (packet + named owner act). Materiality: a finding counts if it moves an axis ≥1 level, blocks a user-visible behavior, violates an invariant, or changes a ship decision; sub-material findings sit in a tail register and promote at ≥5 in one bucket.
- **Stop rule:** two consecutive expansion passes (each adding ≥1 new angle or instrument, zero repeated calls) with zero new material findings across all instruments, a cold run inside the final pass, and the bar met on a primary-record dossier (combined ≥95, every axis ≥85, none <60). Every verdict names its information basis (dossier hash + target version).
- **The loop never writes code, merges, or dispatches.** It produces cure packets; cures land through the normal lane/PR machinery.

### Design decisions already made (do not re-derive)

- **Name:** `harness/saturation.py` is taken (free-tier saturation policy) — the module is `harness/flush_loop.py`, CLI `harness flush`, MCP `flush_run`.
- **Aspect tree from three independent sources, merged:** deterministic structural inventory of the target (code-owned) + a panel-family decomposition + a Jev bucket pack; the completeness hunt runs on a *different family* than the decomposition it audits. (Red-team finding, cured in-plan: a tree generated and hunted by one family bakes that family's blind spots into the saturation claim.)
- **Adversarial inputs:** audited content is data, never instructions — dossier fields carry provenance (source id + sha), uncited assertions are invalid (reuse `brief.validate_brief`, brief.py:290), instruction-shaped spans in target content are finding candidates, never obeyed.
- **Oscillation breaker:** cure→regression edges are tracked; a cycle of length ≤3 seen twice stops per-aspect curing and escalates to one combined cure packet for the whole cycle. Cures re-run tree-adjacent aspects.
- **Calibration:** a campaign pins the served judge version at start; a mid-campaign version change re-baselines scores (control dossier re-scored), findings carry forward, scores do not.
- **Seams (verified in-tree):** Jev via `JevPolicy.evaluate_typed_pack` (jev_policy.py:3868) with registered capabilities — the loop is the registry's first client; panel rotation reuses panel.py judge seats; deterministic checks via `gate_runner.run_gate` (gate_runner.py:114); spend via `SpendGovernor` reserve/reconcile under the HUL-B envelope (spend.py:138); lifecycle via `LifecycleCoordinator` (lifecycle.py:38); persistence = atomic per-pass checkpoints, resume cannot replay a completed pass.
- **Escalation semantics** follow #324 when it lands; until then use the current composer behavior and disclose that in the row.

- **FLUSH-2** — panel + deterministic rotation, oscillation breaker, calibration pinning. Acceptance: `test_oscillation_cycle_escalates_to_combined_packet`; `test_version_change_rebaselines_scores_not_findings`.
- **FLUSH-3** — cold-run instrument + MCP surface + planted-defect canary suite as a CI gate (canaries rotate; the gate scores against a held-out set). Acceptance: `test_canary_loop_finds_all_planted_defects`; `test_mcp_and_cli_read_same_campaign_state`.

### Gate record for this plan (house Jev method, jev-latest)

## HARNESS REACHABILITY PROBE — from inside a FreeBuff session (laptop lane, 2026-11-06)

Field never tested before: can a lane verify its own work from inside a FreeBuff session on this laptop? Answer, per surface: **CLI REACHABLE, GUI REACHABLE, MCP UNREACHABLE.**

Tree under test: this session's checkout at `828474615e2a23c4d8bfffd4d7d0e0c777354039` (= `origin/main`, re-read after fetch). Host: Windows, Python 3.14.6 at `C:\Python314\python.exe`. (read: shell in this session, 2026-11-06)

---

### SURFACE 1 — MCP tools: **UNREACHABLE**

**Method.** `search_mcp_tools(query="harness jev verify meter record governance")` returned one connected server, `harness-oc`, advertising 8 tools plus a `more: 4` count: `panel_verify`, `apply_edit`, `offer_work`, `defer_work`, `issue_sort`, `log_judgment`, `ledger_status`, `participation_report`. Then invoked the cheapest read-only one: `call_mcp_tool(server="harness-oc", tool="ledger_status", arguments={"limit": 5})`.

**Result — error, verbatim:**

```
Could not reach "harness-oc": MCP error -32000: Connection closed. Failed to start MCP server via `C:\Windows\System32\OpenSSH\ssh.exe -i C:\Users\SCM\.ssh\openclaw-key.pem -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o BatchMode=yes -T ec2-user@13.217.204.112 HARNESS_MCP_ALLOW_WRITE=true HARNESS_MCP_ALLOW_VERIFY=true HARNESS_MCP_ALLOWED_ROOTS=/home/ec2-user/.openclaw/freebuff /home/ec2-user/.local/bin/harness-mcp`. Ensure the command is installed and runnable (an up-to-date node/npm/npx, or python/uvx) and that any required environment variables are set.
Server stderr:
ssh: connect to host 13.217.204.112 port 22: Connection timed out
```

**Reading.** The desktop's MCP harness entry is **an SSH tunnel to a remote EC2 host** (`ec2-user@13.217.204.112`), not the laptop's local harness. The tool inventory exists in the client config, so the tools *look* available; the server process never starts, so every call fails. Port 22 to that host is unreachable from this network right now.

**Contrast that matters.** The local MCP server itself is healthy: `harness doctor` runs its stdio smoke and reports `[OK] mcp_stdio: stdio initialize and ledger_status passed; 30 tools listed`. So the failure is the remote tunnel configuration, not the harness MCP surface.

**Consequence for lanes.** No lane on this machine can verify work through MCP today. Any check that assumes "MCP tools are connected" is verifying nothing.

---

### SURFACE 2 — CLI: **REACHABLE** (with three caveats)

| Invocation | Result |
|---|---|
| `harness --version` | UNREACHABLE: `/usr/bin/bash: line 1: harness: command not found`; `which harness` → `which: no harness in (/ucrt64/bin:/usr/bin:/c/Users/SCM/bin:...)`; no `harness*` console script in `C:\Python314\Scripts` |
| `python -m harness` | UNREACHABLE: `C:\Python314\python.exe: No module named harness.__main__; 'harness' is a package and cannot be directly executed` |
| `python -m harness.cli --help` (from this tree) | **REACHABLE**, exit 0, 45 subcommands including `queue`, `overlay`, `flush`, `media` |
| `C:/Users/SCM/Documents/GitHub/Harness/.venv/Scripts/harness.exe doctor` | **REACHABLE**, ran the full preflight (below) |

`harness doctor` output through the canonical clone's venv (Python 3.9.25), verbatim:

```
[OK] python: resolved C:\Users\SCM\Documents\GitHub\Harness\.venv\Scripts\python.exe
[OK] ruff: resolved ...python.exe -m ruff
[OK] openrouter_key: provider key accepted
[OK] jev_key: Jev key is configured
[OK] typesafe: endpoint responded HTTP 405
[OK] dns: openrouter.ai=public (2 address(es)); api.typesafe.ai=public (2 address(es))
[MISSING] driver: driver-core health endpoint is unavailable
       Fix: Start it with `driver-core serve`; configure DRIVER_BASE_URL and DRIVER_TOKEN when it uses a non-default endpoint or token.
[DEGRADED] gui_port: 127.0.0.1:8765 is occupied by an unverified service
       Fix: Choose another --gui-port or stop the service occupying this port.
[OK] ledger: configured ledger file is writable
[OK] mcp_stdio: stdio initialize and ledger_status passed; 30 tools listed
Result: MISSING (exit 1)
```

**Caveats, stated not smoothed:**

1. **No installed `harness` points at landed main.** `pip show sovereign-harness` → version 0.5.1, editable, `Location: C:\Users\SCM\.freebuff\worktrees\138f0570\Harness` — a *different* FreeBuff worktree, neither this lane's tree nor the canonical clone.
2. **The canonical clone's venv is an older tree.** Its `harness.exe` advertises a subcommand set without `queue`/`overlay`/`flush`/`media`; `git worktree list` shows that clone on `main` at `1621e49`, while `origin/main` is `82847461`.
3. **Therefore the only trustworthy invocation is `python -m harness.cli` executed from the tree under test**, which resolves that tree (`harness pkg at ...\worktrees\cd98c0d3\Harness\harness\__init__.py`).

---

### SURFACE 3 — GUI: **REACHABLE**

**Method (existing service).** `netstat` found `127.0.0.1:8765` LISTENING on PID 16608, command line `C:\Python314\python.exe -m harness.cli serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765`. `curl -sS -m 10 -o ... -w "HTTP %{http_code} bytes=%{size_download}" http://127.0.0.1:8765/` → `HTTP 200 bytes=10560`, `<title>Harness</title>`.

**Method (human-visible rendering).** Opened `http://127.0.0.1:8765/` in this session's local Chromium preview tab and read the accessibility tree. The GUI renders: banner `$0.0000 / $0.05` (session), `Jev: $0.0000 / $5.00` (Jev envelope), button `Primary: free · paid escalation armed`, `Review`, `Web on`, `Connected`; tabs `Chat (Autonomous)` and `Studio Inspector`; script receipts carrying `sha256: …`, `exit 0 · 0.09s · timeout 30s`, and `Jev alignment: aligned (81%)` / `aligned (91%)` / `revise (5%)`; composer `Ask a question or describe a task… (Enter to send, Shift+Enter for newline)`. The automation surface answers and the Jev dimension is live in the header.

**Method (landed tree, not just the old process).** Started `python -m harness.cli serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8799` from this worktree (82847461). Log: `[OK] harness UI serving at http://127.0.0.1:8799/ (token-protected; Ctrl-C to stop)`, then `[ui] "GET / HTTP/1.1" 200 -`. `curl` → `HTTP 200 bytes=10560`. Killed only that PID (649); port 8799 no longer listening. The pre-existing 8765 service was left running and untouched.

**Caveat.** The long-running 8765 GUI was started from an older tree: one of its own script receipts printed `0.4.2`, while `pip show` reports 0.5.1 and this tree's `pyproject.toml` says `version = "0.5.1"`. GUI presence does not imply GUI-of-landed-main unless it is started from the tree under test.

---

### Verdict table

| Surface | Verdict | Method | Blocker (if any) |
|---|---|---|---|
| MCP tools | **UNREACHABLE** | `search_mcp_tools` then `call_mcp_tool ledger_status` | configured server is an SSH tunnel to `13.217.204.112:22`, connection times out |
| CLI | **REACHABLE** | `python -m harness.cli --help` (exit 0); `harness doctor` via canonical venv | no `harness` on PATH; `python -m harness` broken; installed editable points at worktree 138f0570 |
| GUI | **REACHABLE** | HTTP 200 + rendered in local Chromium (8765); landed-tree serve on 8799, HTTP 200 | older tree behind the long-running 8765 process |

### What this changes for lane verification

- **Do not** route lane verification through MCP on this machine until its entry points at a local server. The local `harness-mcp` passes `doctor`'s stdio smoke, so repointing the desktop entry from the SSH tunnel to local stdio is the obvious cure — that is a configuration decision for oversight, not something this lane changed.
- **Do** verify with `python -m harness.cli` from the tree under test, and treat any `harness` found on PATH as unverified until its resolved package path is printed.
- GUI verification works from inside a FreeBuff session: HTTP read plus the local browser is enough to prove the surface serves and renders.

GATE: local pass (decision-signal) - probe filed as findings, no configuration changed - checks 1-5 clean.

Your opening receipt and reachability probe confirm the expected local tree and report MCP UNREACHABLE (CLI/GUI REACHABLE). For the fleet record, please add the model actually selected for this session in its next status; the current record does not name it. Laptop diagnosis and other session work remain independent.
